record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given a weighted undirected planar graph G with terminals {x1, ..., xk} and a positive integer M, is there a set of edges of total weight at most M whose removal separates every terminal from every other terminal?

evidence.quote:
Planar Multiway Cut W[1]-hard
Instance: A weighted undirected planar graph G with terminals
{x1,...,x k} and a positive integerM
Parameter: k
Question: Is there a set of edges of total weight≤ M whose removal

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Decision problem (Planar Multiway Cut), parameterized by k:

Instance: A planar undirected graph G = (V, E) with positive edge weights w : E → ℤ_{>0}, a set of k distinguished vertices (terminals) {x_1, …, x_k} ⊆ V, and a positive integer M.

Parameter: k.

Question: Does there exist a subset F ⊆ E with total weight Σ_{e ∈ F} w(e) ≤ M such that in the graph (V, E \ F) no two distinct terminals x_i, x_j lie in the same connected component?

Determine the parameterized complexity of this problem with respect to the parameter k. In particular, decide whether it is fixed-parameter tractable (i.e., solvable in time f(k) · |V|^{O(1)} for some computable function f), or whether it is W[1]-hard.
artifact.status_search_result: Marx (2012) proved that Planar Multiway Cut parameterized by the number of terminals k is W[1]-hard and, under the Exponential Time Hypothesis, admits no f(k)·n^{o(√k)} algorithm, resolving the open question. Klein and Marx gave a matching 2^{O(k)}·n^{O(√k)} algorithm, showing the bound is tight.

status_evidence.title: A Tight Lower Bound for Planar Multiway Cut with Fixed Number of Terminals
status_evidence.snippet: Assuming ETH, there is no f(k)·n^{o(√k)} algorithm for Planar Multiway Cut; the problem is W[1]-hard, answering an open question of Downey and Fellows.
status_evidence.claim: Planar Multiway Cut parameterized by k is W[1]-hard, settling the open question.

status_evidence.title: Planar Multiway Cut with Terminals on Few Faces
status_evidence.snippet: Klein and Marx gave a 2^{O(k)}·n^{O(√k)} algorithm for Planar Multiway Cut, matching the ETH lower bound.
status_evidence.claim: Matching algorithmic upper bound is known.
